Many tracklists write the record label after the title, behind a spaced bullet, sometimes with a note after a second one. 0.7 kept all of it in the title and could move a version past the label. 0.8.0 reads the label into a new field, `label`, in all five ports (rule R8.7).

```js
import { format, parse } from "trackparse";

const t = parse("Scrufizzer & Machinedrum - WHO (K-LONE VIP) • IAMSIAM");
t.title;      // 'WHO'
t.fullTitle;  // 'WHO (K-LONE VIP)'
t.label;      // 'IAMSIAM'

const n = parse("Noisia - concussion • VISION • VISION RADIO RELOAD");
n.label;  // 'VISION'
n.junk;   // [ { raw: 'VISION RADIO RELOAD', kind: 'note' } ]
format(n);                    // 'Noisia - concussion • VISION'
format(n, { label: false });  // 'Noisia - concussion'
```

### What's new

- **`label`** on every parsed track: the text after the first spaced bullet (U+2022 `•`) that follows the artist/title dash, as written. `null` when there is none. It is not the junk kind `label` (`[NCS Release]`), which stays as it was.
- **Junk kind `note`** for every segment after the label (`VISION RADIO RELOAD` above). A segment made only of junk phrases (`• FREE DOWNLOAD`) is junk with that phrase's kind, and junk groups in the tail (`[Official Video]`) are junk as before.
- **`format` writes the label back** as ` • LABEL`. Turn it off with `label: false` (Python `label=False`, Rust `.label(false)`, Go `OmitLabel: true`, C `trackparse_format_options_set_omit_label(o, true)`, C++ `omit_label()`).
- In C, `label` is the last member of `trackparse_track` and `TRACKPARSE_JUNK_NOTE` is the last junk kind (value 9), so code built against 0.7 keeps working for what it already reads. In Python, `label` is the last field of `ParsedTrack`, and `ParsedTrack.from_dict` reads dicts without it.

### Behaviour changes

Only strings with a spaced bullet after the artist/title dash change. No existing fixture changed except by gaining `"label": null`.

- `Mono Code - Traced • DUB` used to lose its artist (the whole title side was read as a dub version). Now: artist `Mono Code`, title `Traced`, label `DUB`.
- `Noisia - Stigma ft. X • VISION`: the featured artist is `X`, not `X • VISION`.
- `Noisia - Stigma • HOSPITAL (2024)`: the year now stays in the label (`HOSPITAL (2024)`), so `year` is `null`.
- `Noisia - Stigma • FREE DOWNLOAD`: the title is `Stigma`, not `Stigma •`.
- `Hey Jude - Remastered 2015 • X` now has the artist `Hey Jude`: the text before the first bullet is split at its first dash, as tracklist mode always did.
- A bullet inside a title (`Song • Part 2`) is read as a label too.
- Rust: `JunkKind::from_name("note")` now gives `JunkKind::Note` instead of `Other`.
